newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK jobless claims to shrink, but pace slow.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK jobless claims to shrink, but pace slow.

text.p: Britain's dole queues are expected to shrink again in February although at a slower pace than in January.

Further labour market tightening could challenge the notion of a slowing economy, analysts said, although they warned that the overall employment picture remained muddied by government initiatives to reduce jobless claims.
The figures are due at 0930 GMT on Wednesday. The Reuters consensus forecast suggests the jobless count fell by 40,000 last month, following a drop of 68,000 in January.
"There is little doubt that the figures have been flattered by substantial downward distortions in recent months," said Jonathan Loynes, UK economist at HSBC Markets.
The introduction of the Jobseekers' Allowance (JSA) and benefit fraud hotline last year are helping to drive the unemployment figures lower.
"Despite these distortions, the labour market is tightening," said Ciaran Barr, UK economist at Morgan Grenfell.
Loynes agrees and calculates that after stripping out the distortions, unemployment is still falling at a rate of about 30,000 per month.
The JSA replaced old-style unemployment benefits in October and requires claimants to provide additional evidence that they are actively seeking work. This has caused a backlog of claims to mount.

The fraud hotline was launched in August and has received over 120,000 calls about people suspected of claiming benefits while working at the same time. Advertisments with the phone number can be seen throughout Britain.
David Bloom, UK economist at James Capel, said the large falls in unemployment are in stark contrast to other economic data which show the pace of growth easing slightly.

"There is no doubt that there are some very good reasons to be sceptical over the labour market figures. While other economic indicators are showing signs of cooling, the labour market data continues to go from strength to strength."
Economists forecast annualised average earnings growth to hold steady at 4.25 percent in January. Unit wage costs are expected to dip slightly to 3.1 percent in January from 3.2 percent previously.
